title: Inside the Data Center Boom: Understanding the Massive Infrastructure That Supports AI

metadata.title: Inside the Data Center Boom: Understanding the Massive Infrastructure That Supports AI

summary: Nick Del Deo explains the distinct economics of data-center property, interconnection hubs, GPU clouds and fiber. The strongest framework separates recurring cash metrics from expansion capex and models CoreWeave contract-level lifetime returns rather than applying peer EBITDA multiples. He expects eventual competition and power supply to reduce scarcity returns but avoids a precise collapse date. Later Equinix growth was stronger than the reported early 2026 plan, while Lumen's legacy decline remained visible.
assessment: Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.
speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman interviews Nick Del Deo. Most forecasts and valuation estimates belong to Del Deo; Eisman asks clarifying questions and restates accounting concepts.
framework_points: Map property ownership, equipment ownership and customer obligations separately.
Distinguish network effects from temporary physical scarcity.
Value GPU projects over equipment life, including capex, financing, renewals and residual value.
Lifetime NPV per invested dollar is not an annual return on capital.
Check final user latency separately from latency inside a training cluster.
Deduplicate utility requests and distinguish planned, contracted and energized power.
tools_and_charts: Capital cost per MW excluding IT equipment
REIT taxable income versus AFFO and cash flow
ROIC minus cost of capital and reinvestment volume
CoreWeave GPU contract DCF and $65 valuation
Lumen conduit value and Cogent wavelength revenue
transcript_cautions: Nick Del Deo and company names are frequently garbled.
Recording appears materially earlier than October 22 publication: Core Scientific bid is described as recent and CoreWeave quoted near $90. Exact date not established.
The $40b equipment figure against a $14b-$15b contract may be a caption or spoken-number error and is not silently corrected.
The 2025 $5.3b revenue and 2026 AFFO path are forecasts at the time, not realized premises.

assumptions: A training run lasts weeks or months and does not require real-time responses to a distant user.
Its distributed compute still requires fast internal communication.
evidence_basis.proof: A small extra delay to a user endpoint is negligible relative to the long training run, whereas slow internal links repeated throughout computation can constrain performance. This distinguishes external location latency from internal cluster latency.
